questions.question: Intersections are usually:

options.text: Safe because there is a lot of traffic.

questions.explanation: Intersections are dangerous because many vehicles meet there. This creates many chances for accidents between motorcyclists and other drivers.

questions.question: A person over 21 with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of ______ is legally intoxicated.
questions.explanation: In New Mexico, drivers over 21 can be arrested for driving with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Driving under the influence is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Riding at night:

options.text: Is safer when you wear reflective clothing.
Is unsafe because other drivers cannot see your turn signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safer when you wear reflective clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials at night so other drivers can see you better.

questions.question: The best way to handle tailgaters is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make rude gestures.
Speed up to create distance between you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes to let tailgaters pass. Speeding up makes them follow even faster, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: In a no passing zone:

options.text: A motorcycle may still pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle may pass if it finishes before another vehicle approaches.
A motorcycle may pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: Passing is not allowed in no passing zones. You also cannot pass by riding off the road.

questions.question: If you wait one hour per alcoholic drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
Effects of alcohol may still remain.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Effects of alcohol may still remain.
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink per hour. However, alcohol can build up in your system even at this rate, and it may still affect your riding ability.

questions.question: An approved helmet:

options.text: Lets you see as far to the sides as you need.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you see as far to the sides as you need.
questions.explanation: Approved helmets allow riders to see far enough to the sides for safe riding. Approved helmets have labels with the maker's name, instructions, and safety standards information.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection usually takes:

options.text: A few minutes and should be done once a month.
A few minutes and should be done before every ride.
Over an hour and must be done by a mechanic.
Over an hour and only if you carry a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: A few minutes and should be done before every ride.
questions.explanation: Do a thorough check before every ride. It takes only a few minutes.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger on a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Have a seat large enough for two riders.
Have only one set of footrests.
Not ask the passenger to wear protective clothing.
Put a sticker on the brake light to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a seat large enough for two riders.
questions.explanation: Only carry a passenger if your motorcycle has a seat for two riders. The motorcycle should have footrests for the passenger. Your passenger should wear the same safety gear as the operator.

questions.question: Boots or shoes should:

options.text: Have long laces that hang loose.
Cover the ankle and give support.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the ankle and give support.
questions.explanation: Choose tall, sturdy boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles. Heels should be low so they don't catch on things. Tuck in long laces so they don't get caught on the motorcycle.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make rude gestures.
Speed up to get away from them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up makes them tailgate at a higher speed, which increases danger.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, where should your feet be?
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests to stay balanced. Do not drag them on the ground. Do not point your toes down because they might catch on the road. Keep your feet near the controls so you can use them quickly if needed.

questions.question: How does a three-wheeled motorcycle handle curves?

options.text: The same as a two-wheeled motorcycle.
It should not be operated in curves.
It should use the shoulder when taking a curve.

questions.explanation: A three-wheeled motorcycle handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: What does a face shield do?

options.text: Does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, impact-resistant face shield gives the best protection for your eyes and face. Eyeglasses or sunglasses are not enough. In Vermont, eye and face protection are not legally required if your motorcycle has a windshield, but they are recommended.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Many surfaces have poor traction. These include wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers. Dry pavement has good traction for tires and is safer for motorcycles.

questions.question: If your motorcycle will take longer to stop than usual, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance on slippery surfaces. If stopping will take longer than usual, give yourself more space between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: Which helmet gives the most protection?

options.text: One that meets U.S. DOT standards.
One that has survived a previous crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: One that meets U.S. DOT standards.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards for the best protection. Your helmet should fit snugly all around your head.

questions.question: When does a motorcycle fit you properly?

options.text: When your feet can touch the ground while seated.
When you can reach the controls by stretching.
When the handlebars go over your head.
When your feet cannot rest on the foot pegs.

questions.correctAnswerText: When your feet can touch the ground while seated.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you properly if your feet can touch the ground while seated. You should be able to easily reach and use the controls.

questions.question: What do goggles protect?

options.text: Your face as well as a face shield.
Your entire face like a windshield.

questions.explanation: Goggles protect only your eyes, not your entire face. A face shield protects your whole face and is recommended over goggles. A windshield is not a good substitute for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders should wear shoes with soles that:
questions.explanation: Wear boots or shoes that are tall and sturdy to support your ankles. The soles should be hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: Switching to a lower gear is also called:
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear acts like using the brakes. This is why downshifting is called engine braking.

questions.question: When alcohol and drugs are used together, their effects:

options.text: Can be stronger than using either one alone.
Are less dangerous than using either one alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be stronger than using either one alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, can make it harder to ride safely. Alcohol and some drugs together are even more dangerous.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Start slowing down later than usual.
Try to fit into smaller gaps in traffic.

questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight and changes how your motorcycle handles. Your motorcycle will speed up slower, turn slower, and need more distance to stop. Ride slower, start slowing sooner before stops, keep more space between you and other vehicles, and wait for bigger gaps before crossing or turning into traffic.

questions.question: Before riding a motorcycle, you should check everything below except:
questions.explanation: Before riding, check tire tread and air pressure, oil and fluid levels, lights, and signals.
